Uses of Interface
org.smtlib.IResponse

Packages that use IResponse
Package
Description
org.smtlib
This package contains the main classes and abstract interfaces for this SMT-LIB tool; the tool provides a stand-alone SMT-LIB-compliant command-line application, an application that responds to SMT-LIB commands over a network port, and an SMT-LIB Java API.
org.smtlib.command
This package contains implementations of the SMT-LIB commands, implementing the interfaces defined in ICommand; these implementations are independent of the concrete syntax that might be used, except that each command object has methods that can parse or print representations of the command in the standard (or potentially other) concrete syntaxes.
org.smtlib.ext
This package contains commands that are extensions to SMT-LIB.
org.smtlib.impl
This package is an implementation of the interfaces defined in org.smtlib.
org.smtlib.sexpr
This package is a concrete implementation of a particular concrete syntax for the abstract SMT-LIB semantics.
org.smtlib.solvers
This package implements various instances of org.smtlib.ISolver, which are specific solvers that wrap and interact with various off-the-shelf SMT solvers currently available.

    Solver_simplify.reset()
    Transplanted from Solver_test.reset(): this class has no real process operation to ask for a reset (Simplify's protocol has no such concept), so this remains an entirely local, client-side reset exactly as it was as an inherited Solver_test method -- it does not, and did not before this restructuring, reset any BG_PUSH state already accumulated in the real Simplify process itself.

    Solver_z3_4_3.reset_assertions()
    z3-4.3 predates reset-assertions (added in SMT-LIB 2.5), and turns out to already handle that gracefully on its own: sent the literal, unrecognized command text, its SMT2 front-end replies with the literal token "unsupported" -- confirmed directly against a real z3-4.3.1 binary -- rather than erroring or crashing.

    protected IResponse
    Solver_z3_4_3_2.set_option_impl(IExpr.IKeyword key, IAttributeValue value)
    Corrects a non-conformance of z3 4.3.2: set-option of an option it does not know answers an error, (error "line L column C: unknown parameter 'foo'\nLegal parameters are:\n ..."), which names the option and then lists every parameter of its module, one per line.
    protected IResponse
    Solver_z3_4_3.set_option_impl(IExpr.IKeyword key, IAttributeValue value)
    z3 4.3 accepts :interactive-mode, :produce-assertions and the other :produce- options after set-logic, which SMT-LIB forbids, so that is reported here; values are kept here for get_option.
